samples: This program prints a directory tree starting from a path given on the command line, or the current directory if no path is provided. For every file and folder, it shows the name and the total size in bytes, with directory sizes computed recursively from all contained files. It is useful if you want a simple text-based disk-usage tree, but it depends on filesystem access and will fail if it cannot read the target path.

This program prints a directory tree starting from a path given on the command line, or the current directory if none is provided. For each file and folder, it shows the name and total size in bytes, where folder sizes are computed recursively from all contained files. It is useful if you want a simple size-aware tree listing, but it requires read access to the filesystem and console output.
